Gauntlets corroded by powerful acid.

Heavy and a hindrance to movement, but better than wearing nothing.
A magic spear that can deal Poison damage. It greatly lowers its owner's Defense.

The two-handed sword Valdes favored.

It is five times the weight of an ordinary two-handed sword, but raises its user's Defense.

A Magic Tool in tablet form.

Raises the Will of whoever equips it.

A Magic Tool in tablet form.

Raises the Defense of whoever equips it.

A Magic Tool in tablet form.

At the cost of its user's Defense, it greatly raises Will.

The name of a devil from ancient myth, said to serve Beal, the devil who rules fire. It became famous through "The Forest of Thorns," a short work by Razuel, a playwright of a century ago, in which it appears as guardian devil of the "Gate of Origin."

The Slave Demons in the ruins, as in the ancient myths, control fire at will. But drench one with water and it can no longer control its flames.

The native people of the continent of Bunia, as the Anoian faith sees them: a demi-human race born of prejudice and ignorance.

The Bumahahaorians that appear in the ruins are cruel yet cowardly, and low in intelligence. They are fiercely territorial and fight over territory even among themselves. Telling the sexes apart is easy: the green ones are male, the purple ones female.

Yet the Bumahahaorians are monsters that should never have existed before the rise of the Sun Empire, for they are a fable invented by the Church about a thousand years ago. So why are they in these ruins...? The questions never end.

The native people of the continent of Bunia, as the Anoian faith sees them: a demi-human race born of prejudice and ignorance. (The real continent of Bunia is no dark continent or continent of death as the Anoian faith proclaims, but a world with a culture and civilization all its own.)

The Bumahahaorians that appear in the ruins are cruel yet cowardly, and low in intelligence. They are fiercely territorial and fight over territory even among themselves. Telling the sexes apart is easy: the green ones are male, the purple ones female.

The name of a small devil handed down in the forests of western Bayreuth. It is said to appear when fish are killed on the feast day of Saint Alba. Before the Anoian faith spread, it was probably a kind of water god (a god who ruled the river's bounty).

They seem weak to cold attacks.

The name of an imaginary creature from the folklore of the mountains of eastern Bayreuth, said to cause accidents in caves and mines.

The habits of the Cave Vipers living in the ruins closely resemble those of ordinary reptiles. Living in dark caverns, they seem nearly blind. Their diet is close to a human's, and they apparently pick out targets by smell. They show a keen interest in human food. Though omnivorous, they seem to favor meat. They are also weak to cold attacks.

In many cultures and religions the ant is seen as a symbol of temperance, hard labor, diligence and communal life. So it is a creature respected nearly everywhere; only in Miranda is it tied to greed, disaster and destruction.

The Crimson Ants living in the ruins seem to bear that influence as well. Their powerful formic acid also works as a poison, and their greed shows in how they behave.

Poison and nerve attacks (Confusion, Charm) have no effect on them at all, but they seem weak to strong acid.

A devil handed down in Krasdar. Not that anyone in Krasdar itself would know it by this name. It became famous through the book of Antonius, a Triestan merchant who wrote a travelogue of Krasdar. The name Indigos itself seems to have come from that merchant's misunderstanding. It is properly Undius, a devil who rules the palace of ice.

Those that appear in the ruins, as befits the name of an ice devil, are strong against cold attacks. Fire can also limit their power, it seems.

The name of a devil from ancient myth, said to serve Beal, the devil who rules fire. It became famous through "The Forest of Thorns," a short work by Razuel, a playwright of a century ago, in which it appears as guardian devil of the "Gate of Origin."
A guardian of Asla Fael. Ajeil is a Malka word meaning "one who assists." (Malka is the second language discovered in Asla Fael.)

What it is made of and what powers it are unknown. But the magic Ajeil uses is clearly fed by a source of power outside it. Its material is a mystery too, with the traits of both living tissue and metal. It resists heat, cold and lightning, and only physical attacks work on it. It also seems weak to acid.

The name of a small devil handed down in the forests of western Bayreuth. It is said to appear when forest animals are killed on the feast day of Saint Alba. Before the Anoian faith spread, it was probably a kind of forest god (a god who ruled the forest's bounty).
They seem strong against heat attacks and weak to cold attacks.
A guardian of the underground ruins. Jacob is a Malka word meaning "one who guards." (Malka is the second language discovered in Asla Fael.)

What it is made of and what powers it are unknown. But the magic Jacob uses is clearly fed by a source of power outside it. Its material is a mystery too, with the traits of both living tissue and metal. It resists heat, cold and lightning, and only physical attacks work on it. It also seems weak to acid.

One of the gods of Krasdar's ancient religion. Like the gods of other lands, those of this land were banned with the spread of the Anoian faith and cast down as "devils," but the "Spider God" was originally a kindly god who guarded a household's wealth.

It seems to have inherited the "guards wealth" part of the legend, for it shows an interest in gems and the like.

It resists heat well but poison poorly. Nerve attacks (Confusion, Charm) also seem to have no effect.

A legendary creature handed down in Miranda. As the Anoian faith spread, many native gods were demoted to evil gods, devils, spirits and the like, and this monster is one of those ancient gods. It was originally a god made by the great god of flame, guarding the fires of daily life such as campfires, but today it is told of as a fire fairy that starts mountain wildfires.

Those that appear in the ruins, as befits a fire fairy, are weak to cold attacks.

Zordis is an Ancient Remus word meaning "child of the accursed earth" or "puppet born of tainted soil." (The accursed earth is land where those who died of plague were buried. Early in the Anoian faith there was no custom of cremation yet, and those who died of contagious disease were buried apart.)

The Zordis that appear in the ruins are nasty monsters that will not die however many times you defeat them (no wonder, since they are already dead...), but they can be destroyed by cremating them.

A guardian of Asla Fael: a soulless sentinel in the shape of a warrior.

What it guards... that seems to differ from place to place, but removing it slows the Living Statue's movements.

Its armor and spear closely resemble those of the Menes dynasty and the Old Kingdom. As for the weapons' design, our civilization is likely the more advanced. Their material is another matter: there, they are clearly ahead of us.

A statue of a goddess worshipped in the Sun Empire. Her name and more remain unknown, but like many goddess cults she seems to exist as a deity of abundance. (A goddess can mean abundance and fertility, and death as well.)

In the ruins, she often has Living Statues guard her surroundings.

Legends of slime-like monsters abound across the continent. Since ancient times water has been the source of all life, humans included, and an object of worship. So for that water to rot was a thing of terror. That fear is surely what gave birth to this Blue Dump.

This monster prefers to live in dark, wet places. Its body is mostly water, and it dissolves organic matter in its fluids and absorbs it. It can apparently break down anything organic, but seems to favor plants above all.

The name of an imaginary creature from the folklore of the mountains of eastern Bayreuth: a one-eyed monster with bat wings. Monsters with bat wings are not rare. Real bats are not as dangerous as we fear, but their black shapes and love of darkness must call up thoughts of the demonic.

Like real bats, it is nearly blind and locates prey by its keen hearing. But it is far more dangerous than any real bat: the sharp claw on its tail can slice through iron armor.

It shows a special interest in gems of all kinds.

A giant snail. Perhaps because their strange shape disgusts people, snails are shunned in Lacone as creatures of ill omen. (Of course, no snails this huge actually live in Lacone.) A mutation, a creature of the devil, or something made by an ancient civilization? The questions never end.

With their distinctive shape and deadly poison, scorpions appear in many myths. Naturally they are mostly cast as devils or the creatures of devils, but real scorpions are timid, and only a handful of species carry a lethal dose of venom.

Those living in the ruins, though, call for caution. They may not be the stuff of myth, but the sharp stinger on their tails can pierce even armor, and a few drops of its venom can kill a person.

Poison and nerve attacks have no effect on them at all.

A guardian of the underground ruins. The name of this monster means "lifeless clod of earth," and it can be found in legends all over the continent. What they all share is dullness and great strength.

Those that await us in the ruins of the Sun Empire have inherited these traits. Without soul, without any feeling at all, they carry out the orders they were given for thousands of years... Might those orders be, as one would expect, to remove intruders like us?

A Guardian with its head detached. With no head attached, its movements are limited as well.
Weak to acid and lightning.

A Guardian Freeze with its head detached. With no head attached, its movements are limited as well.
Weak to acid, lightning and heat.

A Guardian Heat with its head detached. With no head attached, its movements are limited as well.
Weak to acid, lightning and cold.
